D018-D011_h001.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—over and over—about that night at the trainee dorm. I don’t like talking about it, but… it’s always the same feeling, like I can’t breathe, like someone’s holding me down. When I wake up, my heart's racing and I can’t tell if I'm back there or here.  

Dancing used to make me feel safe, like I was flying. Now I just… go through the motions. The choreography feels heavier. I used to stay late practicing, but now I don’t even want to pick what outfit to wear for training. Sometimes the staff taps my shoulder to correct my stance, and I jump like I’ve been shocked. It’s embarrassing.  

I keep thinking, *if only Soojin hadn’t locked us in for "discipline,"* none of this would’ve happened. She said it was a team-building exercise, but we were screaming. I still hear it. I can’t decide anything lately—what to eat, what song to practice—even picking a water flavor feels impossible.  

I know I should talk to someone, but… I don’t know if it’s because of that night, or if I’m just falling apart for no reason. It’s like both—without being either.
D018-D011_h001.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D018-D011_h001.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h002.question:
I’ve been having these odd moments—like flashes—where I’m back in that conference room during the incident last year. It’s not a memory; it’s like I’m actually there again, heart pounding, seeing the sparks from the bot malfunction, hearing the scream. It lasts seconds, maybe minutes, and then I snap back. No warning.

Since then, things feel… flat. I don’t enjoy my work the way I used to, even when a prototype runs perfectly. My wife says I’m distant. I want to feel happy—I see reasons to be—but it doesn’t land. And I keep thinking: *I should’ve recalibrated the safety protocol*. It was my design. Maybe I didn’t do enough.

I feel tense, like I’m waiting for something to go wrong. If someone walks into the lab suddenly, I flinch hard—jump out of my chair once. Lately, I’m misplacing tools, forgetting where I set my glasses. I used to have total focus.

I can’t tell if this is from that day… or just how I’m wired now. Some days it feels tied to the accident. Other days, it’s like the anxiety’s just always there, buzzing under everything. I can’t pinpoint when it started—it’s been about a year, but I don’t know if I’m avoiding things or just… changed.
D018-D011_h002.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D018-D011_h002.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h003.question:
I’ve been having this constant heaviness, like something’s always about to go wrong. Ever since that night last year—the car accident—I can’t hear a screech of tires or see flashing lights without freezing up. My chest gets tight, my heart races, and I don’t snap out of it quickly. It takes ages to calm down, and my thoughts get all foggy, like I’m not fully here.  

Work’s been hard. I used to stay on top of my data entries, but now I’ll sit there staring at the screen, unable to push through. It’s not that I don’t care—I just can’t *start*. My husband tries to help, but sometimes I feel like he’s to blame, like if he hadn’t called me during my drive, I wouldn’t have been distracted. I know that might not be fair, but the fear from that moment won’t leave. It replays—metal crashing, glass shattering—and it still feels horrifying, like it just happened.  

I’m not avoiding things on purpose, and I don’t know if this is all from the accident or just how life is now. It’s just… this constant buzz of unease without a clear reason.
D018-D011_h003.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D018-D011_h003.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h004.question:
There’s this constant tightness in my chest lately—like something’s about to go wrong, even when nothing is. I’ve been jumping at small sounds, like when a server rebooted loudly at work and I nearly fell out of my chair. It’s embarrassing. I’ve started avoiding the office kitchen because people drop pans or laugh too suddenly. 

I don’t know… I used to go out with coworkers after shifts, grab food, talk code or games—stuff like that. Now I just go home, close the blinds, and try to focus on a screen, but my mind wanders. I keep thinking about that night last year—the accident. I was tired, maybe not fully paying attention… I didn’t hurt anyone, but I can’t stop replaying it. I should’ve seen it coming. Should’ve slowed down.

Making decisions feels impossible now. Even picking what to eat or what shirt to wear takes forever. I’ll stand there, frozen. And the anger—I don’t yell, not really, but it’s there, simmering. Like the world’s moving too fast and I’m failing to keep up, and I’m mad at myself for it. I can’t tell if it’s all because of that one night… or if it was building long before that. I just know I’m not functioning like I used to.
D018-D011_h004.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D018-D011_h004.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h005.question:
I’ve been off since that call last fall—the school standoff. Didn’t think it’d stick with me, but certain things… they just hit different now. Sirens, even on TV, make my chest tighten. I’ll flinch hard, sometimes drop whatever I’m holding. It’s embarrassing. My wife says I’ve been distant—don’t talk much at dinner, skip family stuff. I just don’t want to explain how I’m feeling, or worse, say the wrong thing and see her look at me like I’m broken.  

I keep replaying it—how command handled it, the delay in entry. I can’t help but think if someone else had acted faster, it wouldn’t have gone down like it did. There’s this anger, constant, like a hum under everything. Not always at anyone in particular, but sometimes it settles on people I work with. I know that’s not fair.  

Concentrating’s tough. Case files blur on the page. My partner’s been patient, but I hate missing details. I wake up angry, go to bed wired. And if a car backfires? I’m in combat mode.  

But no, I haven’t avoided calls or the job—I’m still out there. And I can’t say if this is all from the job… or just how I am now.
D018-D011_h005.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D018-D011_h005.answer: C & A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h006.question:
I’ve been a security guard for over twenty years—used to be calm under pressure, but lately… things feel different. There are moments, like when a car backfires or someone raises their voice nearby, where my heart just takes off, pounding so hard I can’t catch my breath. I’ll be shaky for twenty minutes, sometimes longer, like my body won’t accept that it’s over. 

There are memories, too—some things from years back on the job, things I don’t like to go over. I can remember bits of it clearly, like the lights or the sound of glass breaking, but whole chunks just aren’t there. I try not to think about it. When it comes up, I shut it down. I’ll change the subject fast or just walk away. My wife says I go quiet, like I’m not really there. Sometimes I feel hollow, like I’m going through motions but nothing touches me.

I’ve snapped at coworkers—cursed out one for a small mistake, which isn’t like me. Afterward, I feel bad, but in the moment, I can’t stop it. I don’t know if it’s about the past or just everything piling up. It’s been like this off and on for a while, but I can’t say exactly what triggers it—just that it doesn’t go away easy.
D018-D011_h006.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h006.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h007.question:
I’ve been running my little bakery for over thirty years—started it with my husband before he passed. Lately, though, things have been… off. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I’ll be icing a cake and suddenly feel like I’m back in that hospital room, seeing him gasp for air. It’s not a memory—it’s like I’m *there*. Lasts just a few seconds, but I drop things, burn my hand on the oven… My staff thinks I’m clumsy, but I know it’s more than that.

I don’t like talking about that time—the sounds, the machines. I push it away. But then I’ll remember random things—his shoes that day, the nurse’s bracelet—but not the actual moment he died. Doesn’t make sense.

When the delivery truck backfires outside, I jump so hard my heart races for ages. Shout at the driver sometimes, even if it’s not their fault. I know I shouldn’t, but I can’t stop myself.  

Last week, I finally got recognized by the local paper for our charity pies. Used to mean everything. Now? Nothing. Just smiled and threw it in a drawer.  

I worry a lot now—about the oven, the rent, my daughter—but I can’t say if it’s been since then, or if it’s always been this way. Can’t tell where the fear stops and I begin.
D018-D011_h007.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h007.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h008.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about a year now—maybe longer, it’s hard to mark exactly when it started. At work, balancing the till, dealing with customers, it all feels like I’m underwater, like I’m watching myself from far away. There’s this one moment sometimes—just a noise, or a smell—that throws me. I’ll be standing there, and suddenly I’m not at the counter anymore. I can’t explain it, but I feel like something bad is happening all over again, though I don’t remember what. I don’t like talking about the past; it’s easier not to go there. Some things… I can’t recall clearly, like big chunks are just gone.

I don’t feel proud of much, even when I do well. Last month I got employee of the quarter, and it just felt… empty. My nerves are always on edge. A phone ringing or someone dropping a pen—it makes me jump, like I’ve been shocked. I get irritated easily, too, over tiny things. My ex used to say I was “wired wrong,” but I don’t know if this is about him, or work, or something older. It’s all blurred together. I can’t tell what I’m even reacting to anymore.
D018-D011_h008.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h008.answer: B & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h009.question:
I’ve been struggling for about six months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to tell. There are moments when I’m in the middle of rehearsal and suddenly I’m not really there; the music fades, the mirror blurs, and I feel like I’m back in that hallway, heart racing, but I can’t see the whole thing—just flashes, like missing frames in a film. I don’t talk about it. I can’t even think about it too long without feeling like I’m going to come apart.  

Lately, I shout at my partners for tiny mistakes—things I’d never have noticed before. Once, I broke down crying after someone bumped into me. My heart hammers for ages, like my body won’t believe I’m safe.  

I used to live for dancing—the high after a perfect pirouette, the applause—but now, even when I nail a routine, it lands like nothing. No joy, no pride. I smile because people expect it, but it’s empty.  

I don’t know what’s wrong. Sometimes I think it’s all in my head because of the pressure. Other times, I wonder if something broke inside me that I can’t fix. I avoid certain songs, certain lights on the floor… but I can’t say why, not exactly. It just feels dangerous.
D018-D011_h009.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h010.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about a year now—maybe longer, I don’t track it too well. Some days, out of nowhere, I’ll be back in that moment… not like remembering, but like *being there*. The colors, the noise—once I dropped a toll ticket because a car backfired and I swear I was somewhere else entirely. I can’t talk about certain things, and I avoid the eastbound lanes if I can—it’s quieter, fewer memories just sort of… popping up.

I don’t remember a lot from that time in my life. Whole stretches are just gone. It’s not that I don’t want to remember—it’s like they were erased. I don’t feel much, honestly. My daughter says I’m “checked out,” and she’s not wrong. I love her, but it’s like I know it in my head, not in my chest.

I get jumpy. If someone comes around the booth fast or from the side where I can’t see them, I flinch. Lights, sudden movements—I’m always braced. And the irritability… small things set me off. A wrong coin count, a driver impatient—I want to snap. But I don’t know if it’s about *that* thing, or if it’s just… everything now. It’s hard to tell what’s what anymore.
D018-D011_h010.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h011.question:
I’ve been having a lot of trouble lately—can’t sleep, my chest gets tight for no reason, and little things set me off. There’s this one flight incident from a few years back… I don’t like talking about it, but sometimes I’ll hear a certain radio tone or see a storm pattern on the radar, and suddenly my hands are shaking, heart racing like I’m back up there. I’ve started switching shifts when I can if I know there’s going to be bad weather. Just don’t want to be in that environment.

I don’t really trust people at work anymore. Feels like everyone’s cutting corners, and when something goes even slightly off-script, I get angry—yelled at a junior guy last month, threw a headset once. Not proud of it. But what do they expect if nobody’s taking this seriously? The job’s dangerous every single day, and most people just shrug it off like it’s routine.

I don’t see the point sometimes. Feels like no matter how careful you are, it’s all just luck. I’ve pulled back—stopped meeting colleagues after shifts, don’t go to the airport bar anymore. I don’t want to talk about it, and honestly, I don’t want to feel it. But the anger and tension? That doesn’t leave.
D018-D011_h011.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h011.answer: C & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h012.question:
I’ve been off since it happened—the accident with the jaguar. It wasn’t my fault, not really, but I keep dreaming about it. Same dream over and over—her breaking free, the shouts, the blood. I wake up sweating, heart going a hundred miles an hour. Sometimes I think I hear screams when there’s nothing. 

I don’t go near the big cat enclosures anymore, even to help out. I make excuses. Just can’t stand being close. I used to love that part of the job. Now, just the sight of the gate makes me tense. My wife says I’ve been short-tempered—snapping at her over little things, cursing when the coffee’s wrong. I don’t mean to. I feel like I’m broken somehow. Like I should’ve seen it coming, done something different. What good am I if I can’t handle my own job?

I keep thinking I’ve failed—not just at work, but as a husband, a man. The anxiety’s always there, low but constant. I can’t tell if it’s about the incident or just everything. It blurs after a while. I don’t know what came first anymore—whether I’m scared because of what happened… or if I’m just wired this way.
D018-D011_h012.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h012.answer: C & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h013.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—some days are okay, others feel impossible. Ever since that incident during the off-Broadway run, I can’t seem to get back in front of an audience without my chest tightening, my voice shaking. It’s not stage fright like I’ve known before—it’s like something deeper, darker. I keep having flashes: the sound of shattering glass, the way the lights cut out. I don’t talk about it, not even with my husband. If he brings it up, I shut down or snap at him—yelling, even—then I feel terrible after.  

I avoid auditions now. Not because I don’t want them, but because the idea of being under those lights, in that silence before the music starts… it makes me sick. I’ve started believing maybe I don’t deserve to be on stage anymore. Like I should’ve seen it coming, could’ve stopped it. The world feels unsafe now—like danger’s always right behind the curtain, waiting.  

I’m on edge all the time. Little things set me off—someone raising their voice, a sudden noise. I curse, say things I don’t mean. But is it just about *that night*? Or has it become everything? I can’t tell anymore. It’s all tangled up.
D018-D011_h013.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D018-D011_h013.answer: C & D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h014.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—maybe longer, but that’s when it really started affecting things. Work is so unpredictable, and with weddings, everything has to be perfect. Lately, I’ll be in the middle of a venue walk-through or on a client call, and suddenly I’m not really there. It’s like I’m watching myself from the outside, or I’ll smell something—like smoke or alcohol—and be back in this moment I can’t explain. It only lasts a few seconds, but it scares me.

My husband says I’ve been snapping at him over little things—a dish left out, the way he talks. I don’t mean to. I just feel wound up all the time, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen.

There are days I look in the mirror and feel like I’m fundamentally broken. Like I should’ve been stronger, should’ve said no, should’ve left. I don’t know if any of that’s even real or if I’m just making it up. The thoughts come and go. But I can’t shake the guilt. I’m trying to hold it together, but I don’t know how much longer I can keep pretending I’m fine.

A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D011_h015.question:

At work, even small things like a guest being slightly upset or the phone ringing too much can make my chest tighten, my heart races out of nowhere. I don’t know why it hits like that.     D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h016.question:
I’ve been having these flashes—like images that pop into my head when I’m not expecting them. I’ll be at work, analyzing samples, and suddenly I’m back in that garage… the smell, the blood on the tools. It’s not every day, but often enough that I get nervous before shifts. I avoid processing evidence from violent cases now; even assigning them makes my chest tight. I requested reassignment, but my supervisor doesn’t understand—nobody asks why I won’t go near certain case files.

I don’t trust people the way I used to. I keep thinking if someone else had sealed that scene properly, if they’d flagged it as active sooner, maybe I wouldn’t have walked in unprepared. I blame the detective who delayed the call, honestly. He prioritized paperwork over safety.

At home, I can’t wind down. Even with the locks checked and the lights off, I’m listening. Always listening. I jump at sirens. My roommate says I look “on guard,” like I’m waiting for something to happen. But nothing ever does. I just... can’t let go. I don’t know if it’s about that one event or just how things are now—I can’t tell where the fear comes from anymore.
D018-D011_h016.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D011_h016.answer: B & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h017.question:
I’ve been feeling on edge for a while—about a year now, maybe a bit less. I don’t know if it’s from one thing or just life stacking up. I keep seeing this moment in my head—out of nowhere—like I’m back on that construction site when the accident happened. The sound of metal, the shouting… I wasn’t even hurt, but I can’t shake it.

I’m not sleeping great, and I get jittery, but I can’t say if it’s that day or just how things are now. Some days feel okay. Others, everything feels tense.

D018-D011_h018.question:

D018-D011_h019.question:

D018-D011_h020.question:
I’ve been feeling on edge for about a year now—maybe longer. I can’t seem to quiet my mind, even at home, even when I know I’m safe. I work alone most days, appraising stones and old jewelry, and I used to love the quiet, the precision. Now I just feel… braced, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen. There are certain things I just can’t handle anymore. I won’t go near repair work if it involves melted metal—something about the smell of torches, I don’t know. I should’ve known better. I keep thinking that. I’m supposed to be careful, attentive—my job depends on it. So why didn’t I protect myself? The truth is, I avoid a lot of things now. Conversations, places… people who remind me. But I can’t say it’s all tied to one moment. Or maybe I don’t want to.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D011_h021.question:
I’ve been struggling for about the last eight months—maybe longer, I’ve lost track. There are moments when everything just… stops. Like last week, while I was arranging centerpieces for a bridal shower, the room suddenly felt far away, and I could hear my own breath loud in my ears. For a second, I was back in that hotel room after the wedding in Asheville—the shouting, the broken glass. I didn’t move for a full minute. My assistant had to snap me back.

It’s not just that. Even when things go perfectly—a happy couple crying during their vows, my husband surprising me with dinner—nothing really *lands*. I see the joy, but it doesn’t touch me. I used to live for these moments. Now I just go through the motions.

And my temper—God, it’s embarrassing. I yelled at a florist because a single rose was wilted. The outbursts come from nowhere, and then I’m left ashamed. I don’t know if it’s all tied to that night, or if I’m just falling apart over everyday stress. I want to believe I can snap out of it, but it feels deeper than that.
